705785.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hékʰō, from Proto-Indo-European *séǵʰeti, from Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ-. Compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀃𐀏 (o-ka) and 𐀁𐀐𐀁 (e-ke-e).

705780.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ekʰinos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eǵʰis (“hedgehog, hedgehog-like animals”). Cognates include Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀑𐀜 (e-ki-no), Old Armenian ոզնի (ozni), Proto-Germanic *igilaz, Albanian esh.

705781.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *h₁égʰis, with cognates including Sanskrit अहि॑ (áhi), Avestan 𐬀𐬲𐬌 (aži) and Old Armenian իժ (iž).

705727.t: Perhaps from Proto-Hellenic *eukʰomai (compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀄𐀐𐀵 (e-u-ke-to, “εὔχεται (eúkhetai)”)), thematized from Proto-Indo-European *h₁é-h₁ugʰ-tor, reduplicated present from *h₁wegʷʰ- (“to promise, to praise”).

705722.t: From εὐχάριστος (eukhắrĭstos, “thankful, grateful”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from εὐ- (eu-, “good”) + χάρις (khắrĭs, “grace”) + -τος (-tos).

705779.t: Likely from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eǵʰs (“out”), perhaps with suffix -ρός (-rós). If so, then Latin exter (< Proto-Indo-European *h₁eǵʰs-teros) is a particularly close cognate.

705792.t: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

705756.t: From ἐπί (epí, “upon”) + ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ, “to stand”). Compare ἐπίσταμαι (epĭ́stămai).

705726.t: From εὔχομαι (eúkhomai, “to pray; to wish”) + -η (-ē, noun-forming suffix).

705736.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “well”) + ὄνομα (ónoma, “name”). Euphemistically refers to "left" because bad omens came from the left side.

705788.t: The verb is clearly related to Old Armenian եփեմ (epʻem, “to boil, cook”) (whence modern Armenian եփել (epʻel)).
